To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanical properties of nanostructures are affected both by surface stress and the reduced dimensionality of the nanostructure.
the mechanical properties of surfaces deviate from their counterparts in the bulk due to surface stress.

(1) the mechanical properties of surfaces deviate from the bulk values and are influenced by the lateral dimensions of the surface structure, (2) the mechanical properties are affected by the surface stress, and (3) the mechanical properties can be measured by contact resonance atomic force microscopy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanical properties of GaN surfaces and nanostructures.
the mechanical properties of surfaces, nanostructures and the influence of surface stress on them.
the mechanical properties of nanostructures and the development of a new experimental technique to measure them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mechanical properties of GaN surfaces are affected by surface stress and size effects, but the latter are not as pronounced as in the case of silicon surfaces, which have been investigated in the same way.
the mechanical properties of nanostructures are not necessarily smaller than the ones of the bulk material.
the mechanical properties of GaN steps are not accessible by the indentation method due to the influence of the finite size of the tip.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CR-AFM is a promising technique to measure mechanical properties of surfaces with lateral dimensions of a few nm.
the surface stress is the main effect that needs to be considered for the mechanical characterization of nanostructures.
we have developed a method to extract the elastic properties from CR-AFM measurements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
surface stress effects can be measured with high accuracy using CR-AFM.
surface stress can be measured by indentation experiments, but only if the size of the indent is larger than the size of the effect of the surface stress.
the elastic properties of nanostructures can only be determined by a combination of simulations and experiments.
